scenario.title: Workflow kinds and routed stages
situations: The user asks which workflow to use.
A change is large but needs one lane; another requires real parallel decomposition.
An existing item is resumed after its workflow has been updated.
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Traced through current intake/routing instructions and catalog contracts, not runtime end-to-end tests.
Verify custom workflows and old immutable pins use the same discovery wording as built-ins.
Command nodes, when present, were checked with installed CLI --help only; this proves parser/help availability, not serving-control-plane capability or successful execution.

lessons.title: Choose by work structure
lessons.when: At intake before creating an item, when the intended execution structure becomes known.
lessons.need: Dash executes a stored instruction; Issue supports planned single-lane work; Epic requires structural task decomposition; Blitz executes a linked document; Task is laneless and merge-free. Size alone does not choose.
lessons.surface: Idea metadata inference; Dash entry; public Workflows and command reference
lessons.gap: Public built-in table omits Task and provides no concise intent comparison. Review question: should the first-work guide teach only the matched choice, with the full comparison on request?

lessons.title: Read the existing item pin
lessons.when: Before resuming, dispatching or handing off an existing item to its next skill.
lessons.need: Use workflows.item.get and its next binding; do not re-file or convert an item to match a remembered stage sequence.
lessons.surface: Workflow item read; skill routing and lifecycle handoff output
lessons.gap: Existing exact references are deep. Review question: should named handoffs/refusals include one stable workflow-reference link after documentation moves?
